The dataset comprises 5,000 Air Jordan secondary-market transactions spanning January 2023 through September 2025. The mean profit margin across all transactions is $82.06, with a median of $35.27, indicating a right-skewed distribution where a subset of high-premium sales pull the average above the median. 61.3% of transactions clear above retail, while the remainder sell at a loss relative to MSRP. The average resale-to-retail ratio of 1.427x suggests the typical transaction commands a modest markup over retail — but this average masks substantial variation by model, condition, and channel, as explored in subsequent sections.

Each point represents a single transaction. Points above the dashed parity line indicate above-retail sales; points below represent losses. Deadstock transactions cluster strongly above parity, while Used transactions frequently fall below.

6. Key Findings & Strategic Recommendations

Key Findings

  1. Condition is the single largest margin driver. Deadstock transactions average $264.01 in profit margin vs. $-57.66 for Used — a gap of $321.67. Sourcing Deadstock inventory should be the top priority for margin-focused strategies.
  2. Model selection matters, but colorway matters more. Pine Green leads all colorways in average margin, while Black Cat trails. Within a given model, colorway choice can swing margin by over $100. The top model×colorway combination (Air Jordan 11 Retro × Pine Green) averages $134.16 in margin.
  3. Channel choice involves a margin-velocity trade-off. Walk-in Retail delivers the highest average margin, while StockX offers the fastest inventory turnover. The optimal channel depends on whether the strategy prioritizes per-unit profit or capital efficiency.
  4. Seasonality is present but moderate. May shows the highest average margins, while October shows the lowest. Timing listings around seasonal peaks can incrementally improve returns.
  5. Over 39% of transactions sell below retail. This underscores that resale is not a guaranteed profit — model, condition, and channel selection are critical to avoiding losses.

Strategic Recommendations

Sourcing Priority

Focus acquisition budget on Deadstock units of Air Jordan 11 Retro and Pine Green colorways. Avoid Used inventory unless acquired at deep discount to retail — the average Used transaction sells $57.66 below cost.

Channel Strategy

Use Walk-in Retail for high-margin Deadstock listings where per-unit profit justifies slower turnover. Use StockX for VNDS or less sought-after colorways where velocity matters more than margin.

Inventory Holding

Average days in inventory is 22.5 across all channels. Listings exceeding 30 days without movement should trigger price reassessment. The fastest-moving channel (StockX) averages 7.5 days — use this as a benchmark.

Timing

List premium Deadstock inventory ahead of May when margins peak. Avoid listing Used inventory during October when markdowns are deepest. Align sourcing cycles to build inventory 30–45 days before seasonal peaks.

Limitations: This analysis is based on 5,000 synthetic transactions designed to model realistic market behavior. While directional patterns should inform strategy, exact margin figures and premium rates may differ in live markets. The dataset covers January 2023 through September 2025 — trends beyond this window are not captured. Always validate with current market data before executing sourcing or pricing decisions.
